yaml.title: DL Tasks

This site is organised by **task** rather than by architecture. The question it answers is "I have this input and want that output, what should I use", which is how the problem usually arrives. The categories follow the Hugging Face task taxonomy, so a page here maps directly onto a filterable set of models on the Hub.

Every page follows the same structure: real-world use cases, recent research, the models currently worth using, the metrics that evaluate them, runnable code, and a benchmark comparison at the end. Where hardware allows, the page finishes with a live demo against the webcam or microphone.

The code is written for a small machine, an RTX 3060 with 12 GB of VRAM alongside 20 GB of system RAM, so models are loaded in half precision, one at a time, and freed afterwards. Anything that will not fit is discussed in prose rather than run.

For the architectures underneath these tasks see [DL Methods](https://bthek1.github.io/DL_methods/).

---


| Page | Task |
|---|---|
| [Text Classification](Natural_Language_Processing/00_Text_Classification.ipynb) | Assigning a label to a document, which covers sentiment and intent |
| [Token Classification](Natural_Language_Processing/01_Token_Classification.ipynb) | Labelling each token, as in named entity recognition |
| [Question Answering](Natural_Language_Processing/03_Question_Answering.ipynb) | Extracting an answer from a passage |
| [Table Question Answering](Natural_Language_Processing/02_Table_Question_Answering.ipynb) | The same against structured tables |
| [Zero-Shot Classification](Natural_Language_Processing/04_Zero_Shot_Classification.ipynb) | Classifying into labels the model was never trained on |
| [Translation](Natural_Language_Processing/05_Translation.ipynb) | Between languages |
| [Summarization](Natural_Language_Processing/06_Summarization.ipynb) | Long text to short |
| [Text Generation](Natural_Language_Processing/08_Text_Generation.ipynb) | The autoregressive case, which is what an LLM does |
| [Fill-Mask](Natural_Language_Processing/09_Fill_Mask.ipynb) | Predicting a hidden token, the objective BERT was trained on |
| [Feature Extraction](Natural_Language_Processing/07_Feature_Extraction.ipynb) | Turning text into vectors |
| [Sentence Similarity](Natural_Language_Processing/10_Sentence_Similarity.ipynb) | Comparing those vectors, which is what retrieval is built on |
| [Text Ranking](Natural_Language_Processing/11_Text_Ranking.ipynb) | Re-ordering candidates, the second stage of a RAG pipeline |

## Frameworks and Theory

| Page | Covers |
|---|---|
| [Pipecat](Frameworks/01_pipecat.ipynb) | The framework for real-time voice and multimodal agents, which is what stitches the audio pages into a conversation |
| [Mathematical Foundations](Theory/00_0_Mathematics_Foundations.ipynb) | The symbols and notation the papers assume you already read |
| [Deep Learning Equations](Theory/01_2_Deep_Learning_Equations.ipynb) | The equations behind the architectures |
| [Discrete Maths](Theory/00_1_Discrete_Maths.ipynb) | Sets, logic, and combinatorics |
| [Physics Equations](Theory/01_0_Physics_Equations.ipynb) | General reference |
| [Electromagnetic Equations](Theory/01_1_Electromagnetic_Equations.ipynb) | Field theory reference |
| [Electricity Equations](Theory/02_Electricity_Equations.ipynb) | Circuit reference |

---

## Not Covered Yet

- **The benchmark numbers are indicative, not rigorous.** Each page compares models on a small sample on one GPU, which is enough to choose between candidates but not to make a claim about a leaderboard.
- **Nothing is fine-tuned.** Every page uses pretrained checkpoints as they come, so there is no coverage of adapting a model to a specific dataset.
- **No deployment or serving.** The pages stop at a working model in a notebook. Nothing on inference servers, batching, quantisation for production, or latency budgets.
- **Large models are described but not run.** Anything past roughly 3B parameters in half precision, or an 8 GB download, is discussed in prose rather than executed, so the biggest models in each category are unmeasured here.
- **[ForResNet](Theory/11_ForResNet.ipynb) is a placeholder** marked "coming soon".
- The theory folder is a reference sheet rather than an explanation, and the physics and electromagnetism pages sit oddly against the rest of the site.

---
